gloss: to pull in hand over hand; to trace back

definitions.gloss: to pull in hand over hand; to haul in; to reel in
definitions.explanation: To draw in something long and flexible — a rope, thread, net, or line — by moving the hands alternately along it.

definitions.gloss: to trace back; to follow (a memory, a lead)
definitions.explanation: To follow a memory, a chain of associations, or a thread of evidence back toward its source, as if pulling it in bit by bit.

examples.japanese: ロープを{手繰|たぐ}って{船|ふね}を{岸|きし}に{寄|よ}せた。
examples.english: I pulled in the rope hand over hand and brought the boat to shore.

examples.japanese: {漁師|りょうし}たちが{網|あみ}を{手繰|たぐ}り{寄|よ}せると、{銀色|ぎんいろ}の{魚|さかな}が{跳|は}ねていた。
examples.english: When the fishermen hauled in the net, silver fish were leaping inside it.
To search back through one's memory.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}の{記憶|きおく}を{手繰|たぐ}り{寄|よ}せてみた。
examples.english: I tried to draw up memories of my childhood.

examples.japanese: {当時|とうじ}の{手紙|てがみ}を{頼|たよ}りに{記憶|きおく}を{手繰|たぐ}っていくうちに、{忘|わす}れていた{名前|なまえ}を{思|おも}い{出|だ}した。
examples.english: As I traced my memory back with the help of letters from that time, I remembered a name I had forgotten.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive; the thing being drawn in takes を. There is no intransitive partner.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糸|いと}を{手繰|たぐ}る: to pull in a thread
- {網|あみ}を{手繰|たぐ}る: to haul in a net
- {記憶|きおく}を{手繰|たぐ}る: to search back through one's memory
- {手繰|たぐ}り{寄|よ}せる: to draw in toward oneself (the most common form of all)

USAGE:
Sense 2 is the one learners meet most often, usually as {記憶|きおく}を{手繰|たぐ}り{寄|よ}せる in narration. It keeps the image of sense 1 alive: the memory is a line you pull in a little at a time until the far end comes into view.

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {手繰|たぐ}っていませんでした
